rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.graph.context-tools.pages`. I read the implementation only to see how pages are prepared and delivered. That showed `GraphSession::dispatch` splits a `read_node` result into 8192-character pages. Each page keeps the same `Dependency::Node` observation. The first page is delivered immediately, and `get_node_page` calls `deliver_page`. Expected behaviour comes from the requirement text, not from this code.

Obligations and the tests that cover them:

- **Graph continuation uses the stored page and records its dependency.**
  - `graph_read_pages_retain_the_prepared_snapshot_after_contents_change` makes the provider swap the node contents to "replacement contents" after the `read_node` call and before `get_node_page`. It then asserts four things:
    - The graph was read exactly once (`reads == [1]`).
    - The recorded inspection dependency is a single `Dependency::Node(Node(1), fp)` whose fingerprint value is the original contents.
    - The page text sent back to the model contains "original snapshot".
    - That page text does not contain "replacement contents".
  - This covers "returns the stored text… without fetching replacement contents", "reading a later page does not observe a newer version", and the recorded dependency carrying the original identity and fingerprint, even when the change happens between pages.
  - `graph_tools_record_delivered_snapshots_and_prepared_pages_do_not_record_delivery` uses 18,000 characters (3 pages) and a `get_node_page` call with `{"page":1}`. It asserts the ordered dependencies (edge observation, then a node observation with the full fingerprint). It also asserts that `finish` carries them into the record and that failed runs record nothing, or only the delivered read.
- **`ToolAgent` records dependencies under `node_inputs`.** The same two tests assert the recorded `Dependency::Node` fingerprints. The assertions also match the "failed read invents no observation" and no-duplicate parts that apply here.
- **Source-read pages retain the callback's dependency without another read.** `source_read_pages_retain_text_and_dependencies_without_another_read` reads a multi-page source and rewrites the file afterwards. It then fetches every page through `get_source_page` with `{"page":page}`. It asserts:
  - Each page's `ToolDelivery.dependencies` is exactly one `Dependency::Node(Node(7), fp)` with the original text as fingerprint.
  - The reassembled pages equal the original text.
  - The observation callback ran exactly once.
- **Discovery pages record no evidence inputs.**
  - `source_tools_forward_arguments_and_present_discovery_and_read_results` forces a multi-page `search_structure` result (it asserts more than one page). It asserts every `get_source_page` delivery has empty dependencies and that the observation callback count stays at 3.
  - `source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads` loops over `list_sources`, `search_text` and `outline_source`. It asserts empty dependencies on the first result and on any pages, and zero callback invocations.
  - Its page loop runs only if a result is actually paged, but the structural case is guaranteed to page.
- **Dispatch shape and return types.** Every test dispatches by tool name with `{"page": id}`. The graph tests go through `ToolAgent` and read the model-visible text. The source tests use `session.dispatch`, which returns `ToolDelivery` with `.text` and `.dependencies`.

Residual points I considered and did not count as gaps:

- No test reads two nodes and then fetches a page of the first. Page IDs are global, so this would check that each page keeps its own observation. The text says each page carries the original node identity, but this is an untested variation of a represented scenario, not a separate obligation.
- Delivering a later graph page records the same observation that the first page already recorded. Duplicates add no information under `node_inputs`, so omitting the record on later pages could not be told apart by any test.

There are no acknowledged gaps.
